_comment: klt erc SUPPLY SPEC for the LDO core -- the artifact T1 item 11
(power delivery, structural) is graded from. See
klayout-tools/docs/design-evidence-tiers.md item 11 and
klayout-tools/docs/cli/erc.md for the contract this file satisfies.
Run it with layout/bin/run-ldo-erc-flow.sh (which also re-derives and
re-checks the substrate assertion below, and runs four falsification
controls against a mutated copy of this file). The committed evidence
is layout/ldo-core/reports/<record>/erc_supply.json.
This block is kind `analog`. Item 11's Analog column asks for this
spec's own run PLUS an LVS report whose reference actually carried the
supply nets: layout/ldo-core/reports/LATEST-LVS's lvs.json pairs both
`VIN` and `0` in its net_correspondence against a SPICE reference, so
the supplies were part of the compare rather than absent from it.
=== WHERE EVERY LAYER NUMBER COMES FROM ==========================
Every layer/datatype below was resolved from TWO independent sources,
cross-checked against each other, per this repo's clean-room rule --
never copied from another PDK's spec:
1. the sky130 PDK's own KLayout layer properties file,
$PDK_ROOT/sky130A/libs.tech/klayout/tech/sky130A.lyp (open_pdks
c6d73a35f524070e85faff4a6a9eef49553ebc2b, the commit sim/pdk.json
pins), whose <properties>/<source> entries name:
64/20 nwell.drawing   65/20 diff.drawing    65/44 tap.drawing
66/13 poly.res        66/20 poly.drawing    66/44 licon1.drawing
67/5  li1.label       67/20 li1.drawing     67/44 mcon.drawing
68/5  met1.label      68/20 met1.drawing    68/44 via.drawing
69/5  met2.label      69/20 met2.drawing    69/44 via2.drawing
70/5  met3.label      70/20 met3.drawing    70/44 via3.drawing
71/5  met4.label      71/20 met4.drawing    71/44 via4.drawing
72/5  met5.label      72/20 met5.drawing
2. klayout-tools' own curated sky130 deck layer table,
src/klayout_tools/decks/sky130.py -- LAYER_NAMES plus
EXTRACTION_DECK's `metals`/`metal_labels`/`vias`/`active`/`poly`/
`nwell`/`tap`/`contact` fields. Same numbers throughout.
One naming divergence, no numeric one: the curated deck's comments
call datatype 5 `met1.pin`/`li1.pin`/... where the .lyp calls it
`met1.label`/`li1.label`/... (the .lyp's `*.pin` purpose is datatype
16). The layer/datatype pairs agree, and datatype 5 is the one
sky130A.lyt's own <symbols> block folds into each metal's net-name
resolution -- which is what `label_layer` needs.
stackup[0] MUST carry `role: "gate"` (klt erc's own contract), so the
stack starts at poly.drawing, not at a routing metal.
poly 66/20 + active_layer 65/20 -- `active_layer` makes the antenna
denominator `poly n diff` instead of raw poly area. That matters
here specifically: this block draws five long poly-resistor bodies
(R_BIAS is 1500 um long), which are real poly with no gate oxide.
Without active_layer they enter gates[] with a tiny non-physical
`gate_area_um2` and report antenna ratios that are artifacts of the
denominator, not a charge risk (klt erc docs, 'Gate area: poly n
diff vs. raw poly area', klayout-tools#1979). With it, gates[]
holds 18 real transistor-gate nets and the sky130 antenna verdict
is clean.
li1 67/20, met1 68/20, met2 69/20 -- the three routing levels this
stream actually draws (confirmed by `klt layers` on the composed
met3 70/20 / met4 71/20 / met5 72/20 are deliberately NOT declared,
and that needs justifying in both directions.
klt erc's docs warn (klayout-tools#1985, whose audit found 7/15/26
false islands on three correctly-strapped layouts) that a supply
whose straps sit on an UNDECLARED level reads as several
disconnected shapes. That warning is about a routed grid whose top
straps were left out; the failure it describes is loud, not silent
-- every extra island is reported as erc.unconnected_net, which is
the very rule item 11 grades on. So the omission fails safe: if a
later routing pass ever puts a rail on met3+, this spec reports it
as a finding rather than passing quietly. run-ldo-erc-flow.sh also
asserts, before every run, that the stream draws no sky130 routing
or via layer this stackup does not declare, so the omission cannot
go unnoticed even for one run.
Declaring them anyway is not free: klt's sky130 antenna-limit table
intentionally does not transcribe met3-and-above limits (they vary
by metal-stack option), so every gate x met3/4/5 pair is recorded
as skipped `missing_antenna_limit` work and the report's antenna
`status` degrades from `clean` to `clean_partial` -- a real loss of
verdict strength on a block that draws no met3 at all.
`label_layer` is how a declared net name in nets[]/ties[] is matched to
geometry. Each declared metal level gets its OWN sky130 label datatype
-- 67/5, 68/5, 69/5 -- because a text only names the level it is drawn
on.
68/5 (met1.label) is the only one this stream actually carries text
on: 28 texts, one per routed net, including the two declared here --
supplies are therefore resolved from met1 text.
67/5 (li1.label) and 69/5 (met2.label) carry no text in this stream.
Unlike the met3+ levels above they cost nothing to declare -- a
label_layer contributes no antenna work and therefore no coverage
skip -- and they mean that a later routing pass which moves a supply
label down to li1 or up to met2 is still resolved, instead of
reporting the rail as unlabeled.
poly (stackup[0]) deliberately has NO label_layer. sky130 draws poly
text on 66/5, but no supply is ever named on poly here, and a
label_layer on the gate role only affects the cosmetic gates[].net
field (klt erc docs, "'Per gate' means 'per gate net'").
One entry per consecutive pair of declared roles, from the sky130 'a via
is named after the layer number of the metal BELOW it, datatype 44'
convention that both sources above confirm: licon1 66/44 (poly<->li1),
mcon 67/44 (li1<->met1), via 68/44 (met1<->met2). via2 69/44 / via3
70/44 / via4 71/44 are omitted with the metals they would bridge, for
the reason given under `stackup`.
licon1 is also sky130's diff/tap contact. That is harmless here: a
vias[] entry bridges the two DECLARED roles it names, and diffusion is
not a declared conductor role (it appears only as stackup[0]'s
active_layer, i.e. as an antenna denominator), so a licon over a
source/drain bridges nothing and cannot make a transistor conduct as a
wire.
This block's two supplies, both `kind: "supply"` so that a short
between them reports as the severe erc.supply_short rather than the
general erc.multiply_driven_net:
VIN -- the 3.3 V input rail (spec/target-spec.md's V_IN row).
0   -- ground. The name is literally `0`: this block's schematic is
netlisted by xschem and its ground node is SPICE node 0, which
is the string drawn on met1.label and the string LVS's
net_correspondence pairs.
VOUT is deliberately NOT declared a supply. It is this block's
regulated OUTPUT, not a rail powering it; item 11 is about the supply
being connected to what it powers. (It is also instructive: declare it
as a supply with the devices[] carve-out below REMOVED and the run
reports a false erc.supply_short VOUT<->0 through the feedback divider
-- exactly klayout-tools#2183's 'device bodies are not wires'. Control
C4 in the record reproduces that on purpose.)
Each declared supply must resolve to exactly ONE electrical island.
erc.unconnected_net fires on zero matches AND on more than one, so
zero findings of that rule IS the 'one island per supply' verdict.
klt erc traces conductor geometry with no device recognition, so a
drawn poly-resistor body on a declared role reads as a WIRE
(klayout-tools#2183). This block has five: R_BIAS (VIN->NB) and the
R_FB_A/B/C feedback string (VOUT->FB->N_FBB->0) plus R_CZ, all drawn
on poly.drawing and marked with sky130's own poly.res marker, 66/13.
Declaring 66/13 as a device body ON the poly role subtracts those
bodies from the poly conductor, leaving each resistor's two contact
heads as the separate terminals they physically are. Verified: the
carve-out removes 878.64 um2 from poly and splits the five resistor
polygons into ten heads.
66/13 is a real PDK device marker, not an ad-hoc one: sky130.lvs
derives res_generic_po/res_high_po/res_xhigh_po off `poly_res`
(polygons(66,13)) intersected with psdm/rpm/urpm, and klayout-tools'
curated sky130 deck transcribes the same derivation.
Both ties ARE declared, and both are graded as checked work. This
departs from what issue #112 assumed, and the reason is that its
blocker has been fixed upstream:
#112 said to omit ties[] because klayout-tools#2169 made a declared
tie join the well/tap regions into the PRIMARY connectivity graph,
collapsing a real design into one island and reporting a FALSE
erc.supply_short. On the klt build this evidence is pinned to (see
layout/erc-requirements.txt) that is fixed: a ties[] entry is
evaluated in its own second extraction, a declared well is never
itself a conductor, and a ties[] declaration provably cannot alter
gates[], the antenna verdicts, or the nets[] findings.
Declaring them is not optional politeness. Item 11 grades a spec
with zero ties[] as `supply_spec_incomplete` -- UNMET -- and grades a
ties_disclosure (either kind) as unmet too, because a disclosure is
the caller's word rather than a computed result. A checked tie is the
only form that reaches met.
nwell_tie -- the PMOS body tie.
well_layer 64/20 (nwell.drawing) is DRAWN here: 26 shapes that merge
into one 17093 um2 polygon spanning x 2217.32..2383.08 um. A drawn
well is a fact about the stream, so it is never subject to the
assertion falsifiability test.
tap_layer 65/44 (tap.drawing) with tap_is_dedicated: true. sky130
draws tub contacts on their own tap layer, distinct from
diff.drawing (65/20) -- klayout-tools' curated deck records exactly
that distinction (`tap=(65, 44)  # tap.drawing -- distinct from
diff.drawing`). So tap.drawing IS tap-only and there is nothing for
tap_requires to narrow; affirming it is what keeps this tie graded as
`checked` rather than skipped-degenerate (klayout-tools#2199).
connect_to li1: the tap reaches metal through licon1 into li1.
net VIN: PMOS bodies are strapped to the input rail.
substrate_tie -- the NMOS body tie.
sky130 NMOS sit in the NATIVE p-substrate: this stream draws no
pwell/tub shape anywhere (`klt layers` finds no 64/44), so there is
no well_layer to name. The declarable form is well_layer: null plus
well_boxes asserting the substrate region (klayout-tools#2255).
The asserted box is [2113.0, -0.5, 2208.5, 80.5] um. It is NOT
hand-picked: it is the bounding box of ((diff - nwell) U (tap -
nwell)) -- every piece of substrate-bodied device geometry this block
draws, which is x 2113.45..2208.32, y 0..80 um -- rounded outward to
0.5 um. layout/bin/check-erc-supply-spec.py re-derives it from the
GDS on every flow run and FAILS if the committed box no longer
covers -- or has drifted loose of -- the derived region, so a
floorplan change cannot silently leave a stale assertion in place.
It is a caller assertion, so it is graded in its own coverage bucket
(erc_coverage.checked_by_well_assertion) and is held to its own
falsifiability test: an asserted region within 1% of the top cell's
own bounding box is rejected as `degenerate_well_assertion`. This one
is 7735 um2 against a 303873 um2 top-cell bbox -- 2.5% -- because
everything outside it is the 2.1 mm poly-resistor field, which sits
over field oxide and holds no substrate-bodied device at all.
Control C1 in the record moves the box into that field and the run
reports erc.missing_tie, which is what makes this a check rather than
a formality.
tap_layer/tap_is_dedicated/connect_to as above; net `0`.
Honest limitation, stated because a met item 11 should not hide it:
this block draws exactly ONE 1.5 x 1.5 um substrate tap and ONE
n-well tap. erc.missing_tie asks a connectivity question -- does each
well/asserted region hold a tap that reaches its declared net -- and
the answer here is yes. It says nothing about tap DENSITY, and a
single tap per region is well short of what latch-up/body-bias
robustness wants across a 2.4 mm block. That is a layout-quality
question for DRC/the floorplan, tracked separately, not a defect this
item can see.
